newsitem.title: Hong Kong: Exiled Chinese dissident arrives Hong Kong - radio.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Chinese dissident arrives Hong Kong - radio.

text.p: Chai Ling, a self-exiled leader of the 1989 Beijing pro-democracy movement, has arrived in Hong Kong for a short visit before the territory's return to Chinese rule on July 1, Hong Kong government radio said on Sunday.
The radio quoted a source close to the dissident as saying Chai arrived at Hong Kong on Saturday to "understand conditions here".
The English-language South China Morning Post quoted the dissident's friend, Ruan Ming, as saying Chai had been granted an entry visa to Hong Kong.

However, the newspaper quoted Ruan as saying Chai had been told to leave the territory no later than May 29, days before the anniversary of the June 4 crackdown on democracy protesters centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
The source said there was no condition on her stay in Hong Kong.
Chai, now studying at Harvard University in the United States, would maintain a low profile during her week-long visit, the radio added.
The visit would be the first for the exiled dissident since she stopped here briefly during her escape to Paris after the bloody Beijing crackdown, the newspaper said.
"We have been advised not to participate in public functions, in particular the march in memory of June 4 to be held on June 1," Ruan told the Post.
"Chai Ling's visa allows her to stay for a week, but I am not sure of her date of arrival," Ruan, a 65-year-old New York-based professor and now a reader at a university in Taiwan, said.

Chai has been criticised for her role in the student-led democracy protest in Tiananmen Square when she insisted the students remain in the square on the night of June 3 even though she left the area.
The movement was crushed with heavy loss of life by the Chinese People's Liberation Army in the early hours of June 4.
Hong Kong's security branch declined to comment on the newspaper report.
